summary.summary_text: ACL Cables manufactures and sells electrical cables and related products in Sri Lanka through its own operations and several subsidiaries/associates (including Kelani Cables PLC and Resus Energy PLC) (Notes to the Consolidated Financial Statements, Annual Report 2024/25). Group revenue rose from LKR 22.62Bn (FY2021) to LKR 37.49Bn (FY2025), +66% over five years, but not steadily -- it spiked 56% in FY2022, then fell for two straight years before rebounding sharply in FY2025 (Statement of Profit or Loss, FY2021-2025 Annual Reports). Profitability has been considerably more volatile than revenue: gross margin ranged from 17.0% (FY2021) to a peak of 36.5% (FY2023), a pattern consistent with a business whose main input costs (copper/aluminium, largely imported) can move independently of LKR selling prices during currency and commodity swings -- the FY2022/23 Annual Report notes the rupee fell 13% against the US dollar that year before FX liquidity improved in H2 (Annual Report 2022/23, p.108). The more durable story across the period is balance sheet deleveraging: total borrowings fell from a FY2022 peak of LKR 6.37Bn to LKR 1.39Bn by FY2025, while total equity more than doubled (LKR 15.28Bn to LKR 36.02Bn) on retained profit rather than new share capital (239,574,720 shares unchanged throughout). Dividend per share has been raised only twice in five years (LKR 0.75 -> 1.00 -> 1.25) and held flat since, a far more conservative payout trajectory than the swings in underlying profit would allow.
summary.gaps_note: This pass covers FY2021-FY2025 Group financial statements only, sourced directly from each year's own audited Statement of Profit or Loss, Statement of Financial Position, and Statement of Cash Flows (own-year figures, not later comparatives). Qualitative business narrative (Chairman's Statement, MD&A, segment detail) was not read in this pass -- causal explanations above are inferred from the numbers and risk-note disclosures only, not confirmed against management commentary. Company-only (non-consolidated) figures, quarterly/interim data, dividend history beyond DPS on the face of the income statement, and shareholder/segment detail are out of scope for this update.
summary.income_statement_analysis: Revenue grew from LKR 22.62Bn (FY2021) to LKR 37.49Bn (FY2025), a 66% increase over five years (13.4% CAGR), but the path was uneven: FY2022 revenue jumped 56% to LKR 35.33Bn, then fell in both FY2023 (-14.7%) and FY2024 (-3.2%) before rebounding 28.4% in FY2025 (Statement of Profit or Loss, FY2021-2025 Annual Reports). Gross margin swung far more than revenue: 17.0% (FY2021) -> 22.5% (FY2022) -> 36.5% (FY2023) -> 24.5% (FY2024) -> 27.3% (FY2025), derived from gross profit/revenue each year. The FY2023 spike coincides with a year the FY2022/23 Annual Report's financial risk note flags as one where "the rupee fell by 13% against the US dollar" before FX liquidity improved in H2 (Annual Report 2022/23, p.108) -- consistent with a cable manufacturer whose main input (copper/aluminium, imported) can decouple sharply from LKR-denominated selling prices during currency and commodity swings, though this pass has not read the Chairman's/MD&A narrative pages to confirm the mechanism directly. Operating profit tracks the same pattern, rising from LKR 2.31Bn (FY2021) to a peak of LKR 9.08Bn (FY2023) before easing to LKR 7.47Bn (FY2025). Net finance income/(cost) flipped from a net cost in FY2021-FY2024 (as high as LKR -1.01Bn in FY2024) to a net income of LKR 444Mn in FY2025, mainly on a sharp fall in finance costs (LKR 1.01Bn to LKR 267Mn) rather than a rise in finance income, suggesting meaningful net debt paydown or refinancing at lower cost (see Balance Sheet tab). PAT is not proportional to PBT: profit attributable to non-controlling interests (NCI) has consistently taken 11-15% of Group PAT (e.g. LKR 840Mn of LKR 5.42Bn in FY2025), reflecting minority stakes in subsidiaries -- basic/diluted EPS (attributable to owners) was LKR 19.11 in FY2025 versus LKR 6.47 in FY2021, a 3x increase, roughly ahead of Group PAT growth (3.1x) itself since NCI's share of profit grew at a similar pace over the period.
summary.balance_sheet_analysis: Total assets grew from LKR 27.22Bn (FY2021) to LKR 43.65Bn (FY2025), +60%, while total equity grew faster: LKR 15.28Bn to LKR 36.02Bn, +136% -- meaning the balance sheet delevered materially over the period. This shows up directly in the liability mix: total liabilities actually fell in absolute terms, from LKR 11.94Bn (FY2021) to LKR 7.63Bn (FY2025), even as the balance sheet grew, cutting total liabilities from 44% of total assets (FY2021) to 17% (FY2025) (Statement of Financial Position, FY2021-2025 Annual Reports). Borrowings did almost all of the work: combined short- and long-term borrowings fell from LKR 3.85Bn (FY2021) to LKR 1.39Bn (FY2025), peaking at LKR 6.37Bn in FY2022 before declining every year since. Working capital composition shifted too -- inventory grew steadily and by far the most (LKR 7.90Bn to LKR 12.47Bn, +58%), consistent with the FY2022-23 currency/import-cost dynamics flagged on the Income Statement tab, while trade receivables were roughly flat to down (LKR 8.96Bn to LKR 7.32Bn, -18%) and trade payables swung sharply -- from LKR 6.55Bn (FY2021) down to LKR 900Mn (FY2023) and back up to LKR 2.13Bn (FY2025), a far bigger relative swing than any other single line, though the underlying supplier-mix reasons for this are not established here. Note: cash and cash equivalents are shown net of a reclassification -- the FY2025 Annual Report split what earlier years disclosed as a single "cash and cash equivalents" line into separate "cash and cash equivalents" and "short-term deposits" lines; the figures used here combine both for a consistent five-year series (LKR 2.53Bn FY2021 -> LKR 7.95Bn FY2025).
summary.cash_flow_analysis: Net cash from operating activities has been positive and comparatively stable across all five years (LKR 2.49Bn-3.93Bn), the only real outlier being FY2023 at the low end (LKR 2.56Bn) despite that year's peak profitability (see Income Statement tab) -- a sign that FY2023's unusually high margin did not convert one-for-one into operating cash that year, plausibly because of the working-capital swings noted on the Balance Sheet tab (Statement of Cash Flows, FY2021-2025 Annual Reports). Capex (purchases of property, plant & equipment plus capital work-in-progress) has been volatile and small relative to operating cash flow throughout: from a high of LKR 511Mn (FY2022) down to LKR 231Mn (FY2023) and back up to LKR 307Mn (FY2025) -- consistent with a business funding modest, steady capacity maintenance rather than an expansion phase. Financing activity is the more interesting story: FY2022 saw a net cash inflow from financing of LKR 2.03Bn (net new borrowing), but every year since has been a net outflow, growing to LKR -2.98Bn in FY2023 before easing to LKR -815Mn in FY2025 -- consistent with the sustained deleveraging seen on the Balance Sheet tab. Dividend payments by the Company itself have been flat in absolute LKR terms for three straight years (~LKR 299Mn in FY2023-2025 vs LKR 240Mn in FY2022 and LKR 180Mn in FY2021), i.e. dividend per share rose only twice (LKR 0.75 to 1.00 to 1.25) and has since been held constant rather than tracking the much larger swings in profit.
summary.equity_statement_analysis: Total equity attributable to owners of the company rose from LKR 13.33Bn (FY2021) to LKR 30.80Bn (FY2025), and NCI equity grew alongside it (LKR 1.95Bn to LKR 5.22Bn) roughly in step, so the ownership split of the Group's equity base has stayed fairly stable (NCI has consistently represented 13-15% of total equity across the period). Retained earnings is overwhelmingly the growth engine, rising from LKR 8.92Bn to LKR 25.55Bn (+186%) on retained profit, while stated capital has not changed at all (LKR 299,488k, 239,574,720 shares throughout) -- no new share issuance in the period; all equity growth is organic. The revaluation reserve jumped materially in FY2022 (to a running balance of LKR 2.97Bn, reaching LKR 3.52Bn by FY2025) following a land and buildings revaluation gain recognised that year (Statement of Changes in Equity, Annual Report 2021/22) and has been broadly stable since, with only small annual transfers to retained earnings (Statement of Changes in Equity, FY2021-2025 Annual Reports). Dividends paid to owners have been the main recurring equity outflow, rising from LKR 179.7Mn (FY2021) to LKR 299.5Mn (FY2023-2025), a far smaller claim on equity than the profit being retained each year -- consistent with a business reinvesting most of its earnings rather than distributing them.
summary.other_statements_analysis: Nothing unusual to add beyond the primary statements from this pass -- segment reporting, related-party transactions, and post-balance-sheet events were not separately reviewed for this five-year window. One item worth flagging for a future pass: the Group holds material equity-accounted investments (share of profit from associates, e.g. Resus Energy PLC) that contributed LKR 70-154Mn a year to profit before tax across the period (Statement of Profit or Loss, FY2021-2025 Annual Reports) -- a real but secondary earnings source that this analysis has not broken out from the four primary statements above.
